swap_risks: CAUTION BANDWIDTH & PHASE MARGIN: GBWP differs by 17.1x (LM358DR: 0.7 MHz p.10 vs NE5532DR: 12 MHz p.4); higher-bandwidth replacements can oscillate with capacitive loads or stray feedback capacitance without an isolation resistor.
CAUTION SLEW RATE DIFFERENCE: Slew rate differs by 16.7x (LM358DR: 0.3 V/µs p.10 vs NE5532DR: 5 V/µs p.4); check full-power bandwidth SR / (2π·Vpeak).

HIGH INPUT BIAS CURRENT SHIFT: Typical Ib differs by 10x (LM358DR: 20000 pA p.10 vs NE5532DR: 200000 pA p.4); high-impedance sensor dividers (>100 kΩ) suffer severe Ib·R DC offset error when swapping from CMOS/JFET to bipolar inputs.

CAUTION QUIESCENT CURRENT SHIFT: Supply current per channel differs by 8.6x (LM358DR: 350 µA/ch p.10 vs NE5532DR: 3000 µA/ch p.4); verify battery budget and total power dissipation across all channels.
HIGH THERMAL MARGIN: Package θJA is 29% higher on LM358DR (LM358DR: 124.7 °C/W p.5 vs NE5532DR: 97 °C/W p.3); re-check Tj = Ta + Pd × θJA against Tj,max.
HIGH MINIMUM SUPPLY FLOOR: NE5532DR requires Vs,min >= 10 V (p.3) vs 3 V on the counterpart; confirm low-battery / brown-out operation still clears the higher floor.
engineering_verdict: LM358DR (Texas Instruments, SOIC-8) and NE5532DR (Texas Instruments, SOIC-8) are Level 2 Functional / Tuning Required alternatives: the PCB land pattern is compatible, but passive retuning or rating derating is mandatory because GBWP differs 17.1x; slew rate differs 16.7x; input bias current Ib differs 10x (CMOS vs bipolar input stage). Signal-chain deltas: GBWP 0.7 MHz (p.10) vs 12 MHz (p.4), supply ceiling 30 V (p.5) vs 30 V (p.3), Vos 7 mV (p.10) vs 4 mV (p.4), Ib 10x gap (20000 vs 200000 pA), voltage noise 40 vs 5 nV/√Hz. Primary bench gotchas to watch: LM358DR "Non-Rail-to-Rail Upper Input and Output Headroom Ceiling" (p.10) and NE5532DR "Internal Back-to-Back Input Clamp Diodes Conduct Above ~0.6 V Differential Input" (p.3). BOM decision: Choose LM358DR when ultra-low supply current (350 µA/ch) is prioritized; choose NE5532DR when closed-loop signal bandwidth requires 12 MHz GBWP. Always verify Pin 1 orientation (TOP_VIEW p.3 vs TOP_VIEW p.2) and official datasheets on hardware prototypes prior to production.
